blocks.value: A `do...while` loop is similar to a `while` loop, except that it executes the loop body **first**, before evaluating the expression.

The expression appears at the end, so the statements execute **once** before it is evaluated. If the expression is `true`, control jumps back to `do` and the body executes again, repeating until the expression is `false`.
Note the **semicolon** after the closing `while(...)`. It is required, and easy to forget.

A `do...while` body **always executes at least once**. That makes it the natural choice for input validation and menus. You have to show the menu before you can know whether the user wants to see it again.
